parsed.doc_summary: SF Rent Board overview of just cause eviction requirements under the SF Rent Ordinance § 37.9(a): 17 enumerated just causes, dominant-motive requirement, housing services protections, and coverage of units exempt from rent limits.

rules.title: SF Rent Ordinance just cause eviction (§ 37.9(a))
rules.requirement: A landlord of a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance may evict only for one of 17 listed just causes, and the just cause must be the dominant motive. Expiration of a lease or a change in ownership is not just cause; removing housing services such as parking or storage also needs just cause.
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction.
rules.key_value: 17 enumerated just causes; dominant motive required
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not give an effective date.
rules.coverage_conditions: Units covered by the Rent Ordinance; includes some units exempt from the rent increase limits (post-June 13, 1979 CO units, Costa-Hawkins-eligible tenancies, some government-regulated tenancies).
rules.interaction: Applies even to tenancies exempt from the Ordinance's rent increase limitations.
rules.penalty: Landlord who evicts or tries to evict unlawfully may face substantial civil and/or criminal liability.

unverifiable_exemptions: tenancies in units regulated by other government agencies that may be exempt
owner-occupancy and other exemptions under the Rent Ordinance
